# Slack / email notify

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P4 · Agents everywhere](../README.md#phase-4--agents-everywhere) · **Lane:** Integrations · **Label:** `feature:user-notify` · **Epic:** [#214](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/214) · **Tickets:** 10 (5S 5M)

Warden can send a message to one person, not only to an alert channel: connect links, parked-request prompts, grant approval requests and grant expiry warnings, by Slack DM or email. Messages go through a durable outbox in cpstate that the CP dispatcher drains. It tries channels in order, falls back when a recipient is not found, and survives integration reloads and CP restarts. Recipients come from a verified-email contact table keyed by user_key, and every action link points to the CP portal. The feature is CP-only and off unless the `notifications:` block is enabled.

## How we build it

- Scope and opt-in. This is CP-only, with no worker or hot-path change. A new CP-local top-level `notifications:` block sits next to `integrations:` in the served config: {enabled: false, channels: [<integration instance names, tried in order, max 4>], kinds: {connect_link, park_pending, grant_approval, grant_expiring, grant_blocked: bool, each false by default even when enabled is true, so every producer opts in through its own kind}, dedupWindow: 10m, perUserLimit: {count: 10, window: 5m}, maxAttemptAge: 15m, retention: 720h}. It is a config.Policy field with json:"-", parsed with KnownFields like the integrations block, so it is never on policyWire or SettingsWire. WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteIntegrations, WriteDetection and the llm-providers writer keep it byte-identical. internal/config checks structure only (names exist in `integrations:`, unique). The capability check runs at CP wiring through the new integration.SupportsUserNotify(type), because internal/config does not import internal/integration. enabled requires --state-dir and consent.publicURL (W-P3-JIT-01). With the block absent or disabled, no outbox, dispatcher or contact writes exist and /policy bytes are unchanged.
- Capability. internal/integration adds an optional `UserNotifier { NotifyUser(ctx, UserMessage) error }`, found by type assertion like Alerter. UserMessage is {ID, Kind, To{Email}, Subject, Text, HTML, Facts []Fact{Label, Value}, Action{URL, Label}}; no sub or user_key reaches a sink. Caps: Subject 150 B, Text 2000 B, HTML 16 KiB, at most 8 facts of 256 B, Action.Label 40 B, Action.URL 2048 B absolute https (http only for loopback). The new assertUserEgressSafe truncates Subject, Text and fact values with boundString and the existing marker, and rejects (never truncates) an oversized or non-https URL or a CR/LF in the email. Typed errors live in internal/integration so callers can test them: ErrRecipientNotFound, RetryAfterError{After}, PermanentError, and ErrorClass(err) returning the closed set recipient_not_found|rate_limited|auth|transport|rejected. Error messages never contain the recipient. Router.Bind accepts UserNotifier-only instances (status connected, no 'no wired capability' warning, no alert queue unless it is also an Alerter), and the new Manager.UserNotifier(name) returns the live instance. Router.Deliver and the alert path are unchanged.
- Slack integration (new internal/integration/slack, type `slack`). Config: botToken as ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN} (expanded at Start, never logged or shown in InstanceStatuses), optional alertChannel, apiBaseURL (default https://slack.com/api, https only except loopback for tests). Required bot scopes are chat:write, im:write and users:read.email. NotifyUser calls users.lookupByEmail through a bounded cache (10k entries, 24h positive, 1h negative) keyed by sha256(lowercased email) with singleflight, then conversations.open and chat.postMessage with Block Kit: escaped text (&, < and > escaped in every interpolated field), a facts section and one URL button, with unfurl_links=false, unfurl_media=false and link_names=false. ok:false users_not_found, or a deleted, bot or app user, gives ErrRecipientNotFound; ratelimited or HTTP 429 gives RetryAfterError; invalid_auth, not_authed and account_inactive give PermanentError. Alerter is implemented only when alertChannel is set. The existing dashboard catalog entry drops appToken and the required channel field.
- Email integration (new internal/integration/email, type `email`, UserNotifier only). Config: host, port (default 587), from (net/mail.ParseAddress), fromName, username, password as ${SMTP_PASSWORD}, tls: starttls (default) | implicit | none, allowInsecure. tls: none needs allowInsecure: true and a loopback host. The client drives smtp.NewClient by hand: STARTTLS must be advertised, tls.Config{ServerName, MinVersion TLS 1.2}, PlainAuth only after TLS, and the whole session is bounded by the ctx deadline. Messages are multipart/alternative (text and html/template output), Subject encoded with mime.QEncoding, CR and LF rejected in every header value, Message-ID <UserMessage.ID@from-domain>, Auto-Submitted: auto-generated. RCPT 550/551/553 gives ErrRecipientNotFound, other 5xx PermanentError, 4xx and network errors are retryable.
- Recipient contacts. New package internal/contacts with cpstate migration `contacts/0001`: user_contacts(user_key PK, iss, sub, email, email_verified, source portal|console|jit, updated_at), where user_key = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) (W-P3-CSIG-06). Rows are upserted only from verified identities: the portal callback (W-P3-CSIG-02), the console OIDC callback (W-P1-SSO-03) and W-P3-JIT-01 pending creation, which re-verifies the Warden token whose email and email_verified claims come from W-P2-TOKX-02. Email is stored lowercased and only when email_verified is true; an unverified login never overwrites a verified email. The table sits behind a Directory interface so p5-postgres-ha can replace it. The offboarding contain step (W-P3-OFFB-01) deletes the row, and upsert failures never fail a login or a pending.
- Notify service (new internal/notify, CP). `Service.Send(ctx, Request{Kind, UserKey, Ref, Params})` returns (id, outcome, error) and never waits for delivery. Kinds are a closed registry: each has a typed Params struct (no map[string]any), a dedup family, embedded text/template and html/template files, and a fixed action path. The action URL is always consent.publicURL plus that path (/portal/connect/<pending_id> for connect_link and park_pending, /portal/grants/<grant_id> (the W-P4-DGR-03 page) for grant kinds); the caller never passes a URL, and the URL never carries status_token or a query string. Template overrides are not in P4. Send runs one transaction on the cpstate `notify_outbox(id, user_key, kind, family, ref, params_json, state queued|sending|sent|dead|suppressed, channel_idx, attempts, next_attempt_at, lease_until, last_outcome, error_class, created_at, updated_at)`: a row for the same (user_key, family, ref) created inside the family's window returns outcome deduped, and more than perUserLimit rows for the user in the window returns rate_limited. Both are written as suppressed rows so the portal can show 'not notified'. No email and no rendered text are stored.
- Dispatcher. One CP goroutine leases due rows (lease_until, so a later second replica cannot double-send) and checks before every attempt: (1) the kind is still enabled; (2) the Ref resolver registered by the producer says the pending or grant is still actionable and at least 60s from expiry, otherwise outcome obsolete; (3) the user is not blocked in the BlockStore (W-P1-BLOCK-03), otherwise suppressed; (4) user_contacts has a verified email, otherwise no_recipient. It renders at send time, computing relative expiry on the CP clock, and calls Manager.UserNotifier(channels[channel_idx]) through alertpipeline.Pipeline.CurrentManager(), so integration reloads lose nothing. ErrRecipientNotFound moves to the next channel (outcome fallback) without retry. Retryable errors back off exponentially from 1s to 5m or follow Retry-After. PermanentError moves to the next channel. Past maxAttemptAge or after the last channel the row is marked dead. If the CP is down nothing is sent, and the outbox resumes on restart.
- Producers. connect_link is enqueued only by the create branch of W-P3-JIT-01 (never on reuse or already_granted), after the pending row commits, as one INSERT that never fails or delays the pending response. Its Params come only from the pending_authorizations row (user_key, agent_id, provider, capped scopes, request method, request host, expires_at) plus the agent registry display name and the provider display name. request_path, mcp_tool arguments, reason and any worker- or agent-supplied text are never used. ref = pending:<id>. Before enqueueing, the producer claims the pending with a compare-and-set on a new pending_authorizations.notified_at column (UPDATE ... SET notified_at=? WHERE id=? AND notified_at IS NULL), so one pending gets at most one message ever, whatever the kind; park_pending (W-P4-PARK-02) reuses this claim through a KindSelector seam and also shares ref pending:<id> and the pending dedup family as a second guard. grant_approval (p4-grants request), grant_expiring and grant_blocked (W-P4-DGR-09) use ref grant:<id> with their own families; grant_blocked uses a fixed 24h window and grant_expiring a 7d window. Those producers live in their own features; this feature registers their kinds, Params and templates.
- Failure isolation and alerts. Recipient errors never raise alerts and never dead-letter in the alert Store. After 5 consecutive auth or transport failures on one channel, notify publishes a Finding `notify_channel_down:<instance>` on the integration Bus whose Evidence is the fixed class (auth|transport|rate_limited) with no error text and no email, using the same self-loop guard pattern as integration_down. If Slack is down, delivery falls back to email. If the IdP is down, sends still work because contacts are local, and the portal asks the user to sign in again.
- Observability. In-memory nil-safe CP counters, exported later by W-P5-RETN-06: warden_cp_notify_total{kind, channel, outcome} with outcome sent|fallback|retried|dead|deduped|rate_limited|obsolete|suppressed|no_recipient|enqueue_failed, plus outbox depth and oldest-due-age gauges. Labels are kind names, configured instance names and closed enums, never sub, email or user_key. The machine-event log line `warden.notify.v1` (msg notify_delivery) carries message id, kind, ref, channel, outcome and attempts only. Outbox rows older than notifications.retention are pruned by the CP retention ticker. Admin audit (W-P1-AAUD-02) records only notifications config writes and console test-sends, not system sends.
- Console and portal. The admin-only console page (W-P1-SSO-05 authz rows, audited) reads and writes the notifications block through a new Server.WriteNotifications, previews each kind with fixture data, and sends a test (POST /dashboard/api/notifications/test, 5 per minute per session) to the signed-in admin's verified email; without one (console.auth none or break-glass) it returns 409 no_recipient. Per-channel counters show next to InstanceStatuses. The portal pending landing page (W-P3-PORT-03) shows the latest outcome for its ref, visible only to the owner. A per-user channel order preference is a separate portal ticket.
- Security invariants. No message carries a token, status_token, secret Reference, request body, query string, request path, or the sub or email of anyone other than the recipient. Links open only the CP portal, where GET is read-only and connect, continue, decline and approve are CSRF-protected POSTs (W-P3-PORT-03), so link scanners and unfurlers cannot act, and the landing page's owner check makes a forwarded message useless to others. Integration credentials stay in CP env as ${ENV} and never reach workers, because integrations and notifications are json:"-".

## Done when

With a CP running consent, the OAuth broker, the portal and JIT, a `notifications` block enabled with channels [slack, email] and kinds.connect_link true, a fake Slack API, a fake SMTP server, and the reference Dex stack where alice has a verified email: (1) an agent request for alice that misses a grant creates one pending and, within 5s, alice gets exactly one Slack DM whose button opens consent.publicURL/portal/connect/<pending_id> and works end to end; (2) with alice unknown to the fake Slack API, the same flow delivers one email with the same link; (3) a second JIT miss for the same pending within 10 minutes sends nothing; (4) a message queued while both channels fail is delivered after a CP restart, or dropped as obsolete if the pending was completed meanwhile; (5) blocked users and users without a verified email get nothing; (6) the console integrations view shows per-channel sent, fallback, retried, dead and deduped counts; (7) no Slack or SMTP payload, log line or alert contains a token, status_token, query string, request path or another user's identity, and no alert contains an email address; (8) with the block absent, /policy bytes and all existing integration tests are unchanged. Grant and park messages are proven in p4-grants and p4-park.

### 1/10 · W-P4-NTFY-01

**Add UserNotifier capability, typed delivery errors and user-notifier binding**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#215](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/215)

Add the library pieces in internal/integration that every user-facing sink and the notify dispatcher need: the UserNotifier interface, a bounded UserMessage, typed delivery errors and a capability check by type. Router.Bind today skips any instance without Alerter, so an email-only instance could never be used; this ticket makes such instances bind and exposes them through Manager. Delivery itself is done by the internal/notify dispatcher (W-P4-NTFY-04), so the alert queue, backoff and dead-letter paths stay unchanged. Nothing implements UserNotifier yet, so merging changes no behaviour.

**Requirements**

- New `UserNotifier { NotifyUser(ctx context.Context, m UserMessage) error }` in internal/integration/integration.go, discovered by type assertion like Alerter.
- New UserMessage{ID, Kind, To{Email}, Subject, Text, HTML, Facts []Fact{Label, Value}, Action{URL, Label}} with no sub or user_key field. Caps: Subject 150 B, Text 2000 B, HTML 16 KiB, at most 8 facts with 256 B values, Action.Label 40 B, Action.URL 2048 B, Email 254 B.
- New assertUserEgressSafe truncates Subject, Text and fact values with boundString and the existing truncation marker, and returns an error (no truncation) for a URL over the cap, a URL that is not absolute https (http allowed only for a loopback host), or an email containing CR or LF.
- New typed errors ErrRecipientNotFound, RetryAfterError{After time.Duration} and PermanentError, plus ErrorClass(err) returning only recipient_not_found|rate_limited|auth|transport|rejected. Error strings never include the recipient email.
- Router.Bind binds an instance that implements Alerter, UserNotifier or both. A UserNotifier-only instance gets status connected, no 'no wired capability' warning and no alert queue. Alert routing, queueing, retries and integration_down are unchanged.
- New Manager.UserNotifier(name) (UserNotifier, bool) returns the live started instance, and InstanceStatus gains Capabilities []string (alert, user). New registry function SupportsUserNotify(typ string) bool builds the instance from its factory and type-asserts without calling Start.

**Implementation plan**

1. Edit internal/integration/integration.go: add the UserNotifier interface next to Alerter.
2. New internal/integration/usermsg.go: UserMessage, Fact, the cap constants and assertUserEgressSafe, reusing boundString from types.go.
3. New internal/integration/errors.go: ErrRecipientNotFound, RetryAfterError, PermanentError and ErrorClass.
4. Edit internal/integration/router.go Bind: keep a binding for UserNotifier-only instances and start the alert drain only when the instance is an Alerter.
5. Edit internal/integration/manager.go: add Manager.UserNotifier(name) and fill InstanceStatus.Capabilities. Edit internal/integration/registry.go: add SupportsUserNotify.
6. Tests: usermsg_test.go (TestUserEgressSafe), errors_test.go (TestErrorClass), router_test.go (TestBind_UserNotifierOnly, TestAlertPathUnchanged), registry_test.go (TestSupportsUserNotify).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a Text of 5000 bytes, assertUserEgressSafe returns a Text of at most 2000 bytes ending in the marker. Given an http non-loopback URL or an email containing "\r\n", it returns an error: `go test ./internal/integration -run TestUserEgressSafe`
- [ ] Given a fake instance that implements only UserNotifier, Manager.Start binds it, InstanceStatuses shows it connected with Capabilities [user], and Manager.UserNotifier returns it: `go test ./internal/integration -run TestBind_UserNotifierOnly`
- [ ] SupportsUserNotify("webhook") is false and is true for a test type registered with a UserNotifier factory: `go test ./internal/integration -run TestSupportsUserNotify`
- [ ] A RetryAfterError and a wrapped ErrRecipientNotFound map to rate_limited and recipient_not_found, and the error strings of all typed errors built from an email recipient do not contain that email: `go test ./internal/integration -run TestErrorClass`
- [ ] All existing alert routing tests pass unchanged: `go test -race ./internal/integration/...`

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-NTFY-02`](user-notify.md#210--w-p4-ntfy-02) Add Slack integration with DM delivery by email lookup; [`W-P4-NTFY-03`](user-notify.md#310--w-p4-ntfy-03) Add SMTP email integration; [`W-P4-NTFY-04`](user-notify.md#410--w-p4-ntfy-04) Add notify service with durable outbox, dispatcher, templates and dedup

### 2/10 · W-P4-NTFY-02

**Add Slack integration with DM delivery by email lookup**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#216](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/216)

Create internal/integration/slack registered as `slack`, implementing UserNotifier (DM to the user found by verified email) and, when alertChannel is set, Alerter. The dashboard catalog already lists a `slack` type gated on IsRegistered, so registering it makes it available. The bot token is a ${ENV} reference expanded on the CP and is never logged. Slack errors are mapped to the typed errors from W-P4-NTFY-01 so the dispatcher can fall back or honour Retry-After.

**Requirements**

- Package internal/integration/slack registers `slack` in init() and is blank-imported in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go next to webhook. Config: botToken ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN} (required, expanded at Start), alertChannel (optional), apiBaseURL (default https://slack.com/api; https only, loopback http allowed for tests), lookupTTL 24h, negativeTTL 1h.
- Required bot scopes are chat:write, im:write and users:read.email, documented in the package doc. Start validates config without network calls; an optional verifyOnStart: true runs auth.test.
- NotifyUser: users.lookupByEmail through a bounded cache (10k entries, keyed by sha256 of the lowercased email, singleflight per key), then conversations.open and chat.postMessage with Block Kit (section with escaped text, facts section, one actions block with a single URL button) and unfurl_links=false, unfurl_media=false, link_names=false. The top-level text fallback includes the URL.
- &, < and > are escaped in every interpolated field, and the URL appears only in the button and the fallback link.
- Error mapping: users_not_found or a user with deleted, is_bot or is_app_user set gives ErrRecipientNotFound and is negatively cached; ratelimited or HTTP 429 gives RetryAfterError from Retry-After; invalid_auth, not_authed, account_inactive and not_allowed_token_type give PermanentError; 5xx and network errors are retryable.
- The token is sent only as an Authorization: Bearer header to apiBaseURL and never appears in logs, errors or InstanceStatuses. Errors carry the Slack error code and HTTP status only.
- Alert() posts a bounded summary to alertChannel and exists only when alertChannel is set. The catalog entry in internal/dashboard/dashboard_integrations.go drops appToken, makes the channel field optional and renames it alertChannel.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/integration/slack/slack.go: Config, factory registration, Start (expand ${ENV}, validate apiBaseURL), and a wrapper type that adds Alert only when alertChannel is set.
2. New internal/integration/slack/client.go: net/http client with a 5s timeout and a capped response body, lookupByEmail with the cache and singleflight, openDM, postMessage, and the ok:false error mapping.
3. New internal/integration/slack/blocks.go: escape helper and Block Kit builder from UserMessage.
4. Edit cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: blank import of the slack package. Edit internal/dashboard/dashboard_integrations.go: update the slack catalog entry.
5. Tests in internal/integration/slack/slack_test.go against an httptest fake Slack API: TestNotifyUserDMBlocks, TestNotifyUserNotFound, TestRetryAfter, TestMrkdwnEscaping, TestNoSecretLeak, TestAlertChannelPost.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given the fake returns users_not_found, NotifyUser returns an error where errors.Is(err, integration.ErrRecipientNotFound), and a second call within 1h makes no lookup request: `go test ./internal/integration/slack -run TestNotifyUserNotFound`
- [ ] Given a known email, the chat.postMessage body has one actions block with a button whose url equals Action.URL, unfurl_links is false, and a second call within 24h makes no users.lookupByEmail request: `go test ./internal/integration/slack -run TestNotifyUserDMBlocks`
- [ ] Given HTTP 429 with Retry-After: 30, NotifyUser returns a RetryAfterError with After of 30s: `go test ./internal/integration/slack -run TestRetryAfter`
- [ ] Given a fact value "<https://evil|click>", the posted text contains "&lt;https://evil|click&gt;": `go test ./internal/integration/slack -run TestMrkdwnEscaping`
- [ ] Given SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-secret and an invalid_auth reply, neither the error nor captured slog output contains "xoxb-secret" or the recipient email, and the dashboard catalog reports slack available with no appToken field: `go test ./internal/integration/slack -run TestNoSecretLeak && go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestIntegrationCatalog`

### 3/10 · W-P4-NTFY-03

**Add SMTP email integration**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#217](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/217)

Create internal/integration/email registered as `email`, implementing UserNotifier only. It sends multipart text and HTML mail over required STARTTLS or implicit TLS, with the password as a ${ENV} reference and headers protected against injection. Message-ID comes from UserMessage.ID so a retried send is recognisable as the same message. SMTP replies are mapped to the typed errors from W-P4-NTFY-01.

**Requirements**

- Package internal/integration/email registers `email`, is blank-imported in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go, and gets a catalog entry in internal/dashboard/dashboard_integrations.go with password as an env, secret field.
- Config: host, port (default 587), from (must parse with net/mail.ParseAddress), fromName, username, password ${SMTP_PASSWORD} (expanded at Start), tls: starttls (default) | implicit | none, allowInsecure (default false). tls: none fails Start unless allowInsecure is true and host is loopback.
- Transport: net.Dialer and the whole SMTP session bounded by the ctx deadline (10s default), smtp.NewClient driven by hand. With starttls the server must advertise STARTTLS, otherwise PermanentError before AUTH or MAIL. tls.Config{ServerName: host, MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12}. PlainAuth only after TLS or on loopback.
- Message: multipart/alternative with text/plain and text/html parts in UTF-8. Subject encoded with mime.QEncoding, Date, Message-ID <UserMessage.ID@from-domain>, Auto-Submitted: auto-generated. CR or LF in To, From, fromName or Subject gives PermanentError before dialing.
- Errors: RCPT 550/551/553 gives ErrRecipientNotFound, other 5xx PermanentError, 4xx and network errors retryable. Error strings carry the SMTP code and host only, never the password, username, recipient or body.
- Logging is debug level only, with instance, message id, SMTP code and duration; no recipient, body or credentials at any level.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/integration/email/email.go: Config, validation, factory registration and Start.
2. New internal/integration/email/send.go: dial (plain or implicit TLS), Hello, required StartTLS, PlainAuth, Mail, Rcpt, Data, Quit, and the reply-code mapping.

### 4/10 · W-P4-NTFY-04

**Add notify service with durable outbox, dispatcher, templates and dedup**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#218](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/218)

Create internal/notify, the CP service that turns a (kind, user_key, ref, params) request into a message and delivers it. Requests go into a durable cpstate outbox, and one dispatcher leases due rows, re-checks that the message is still wanted, and calls the configured UserNotifier instances in order with fallback and Retry-After support. This replaces the in-memory router queue for user messages, which drops entries on reload and cannot report a per-attempt result. The package is tested with fake notifiers and is not wired into the CP until W-P4-NTFY-08.

**Requirements**

- `Service.Send(ctx, Request{Kind, UserKey, Ref, Params})` returns (id, outcome, error) and never waits for delivery. Kinds are a closed registry (connect_link, park_pending, grant_approval, grant_expiring, grant_blocked, test), each with a typed Params struct, a dedup family and window, embedded text/template and html/template files, and a fixed action path. A Params value that does not match its kind is an error.
- The action URL is built by the service as publicURL plus the kind's path (/portal/connect/<pending_id> for connect_link and park_pending; /portal/grants/<grant_id>, the W-P4-DGR-03 page, for grant kinds) and is never accepted from the caller. It has no query string. Template overrides are not supported.
- cpstate migration `notify/0001` adds notify_outbox(id, user_key, kind, family, ref, params_json, state, channel_idx, attempts, next_attempt_at, lease_until, last_outcome, error_class, created_at, updated_at) with indexes on (user_key, family, ref, created_at) and (state, next_attempt_at). No email and no rendered text are stored. Rows older than retention are pruned by a Prune(before) call.
- Dedup and limit, in one transaction: a row for (user_key, family, ref) inside the family window returns outcome deduped (connect_link and park_pending share the pending family with dedupWindow; grant_blocked uses 24h, grant_expiring 7d). More than perUserLimit.count rows for the user inside perUserLimit.window returns rate_limited. Both write a suppressed row.
- Dispatcher: one goroutine leases due rows with lease_until and, before each attempt, checks the kind is enabled, the registered RefResolver reports the ref still actionable and at least 60s from expiry (else obsolete), the Suppressor (BlockStore adapter) does not block the user (else suppressed), and the contacts Directory has a verified email (else no_recipient). It renders at send time and calls the UserNotifier from a ChannelSource looked up on every attempt.
- Outcomes: ErrRecipientNotFound and PermanentError move to the next channel (fallback); retryable errors back off 1s doubling to 5m, or follow RetryAfterError; past maxAttemptAge or after the last channel the row is dead. Five consecutive auth or transport failures on one channel publish Finding notify_channel_down:<instance> with Evidence limited to the ErrorClass value.
- Counters warden_cp_notify_total{kind, channel, outcome} and outbox depth and oldest-due gauges are in-memory and nil-safe. The `warden.notify.v1` log line (msg notify_delivery) has id, kind, ref, channel, outcome and attempts only; system sends are machine events recorded in notify_outbox and this line, never in the admin audit chain, never email, user_key, text or URL.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/notify/kinds.go: Kind constants, Params structs (for example ConnectLinkParams{PendingID, AgentName, ProviderName, Scopes, Method, Host, ExpiresAt}), family and window table, and action path builders.
2. New internal/notify/templates/*.txt.tmpl and *.html.tmpl embedded with embed.FS; new render.go builds an integration.UserMessage and runs integration.assertUserEgressSafe (exported as AssertUserEgressSafe in this ticket if needed).
3. New internal/notify/outbox.go: the notify/0001 migration registered for cpstate.Open (W-P1-SSO-01), Enqueue with dedup and limit in one transaction, Lease, Complete, Reschedule and Prune.
4. New internal/notify/service.go: Service, Config, Send, and interfaces Directory (from internal/contacts), RefResolver, Suppressor and ChannelSource.
5. New internal/notify/dispatcher.go: lease loop, pre-attempt checks, channel walk, backoff, channel-down Finding and counters.
6. Tests with fake UserNotifiers in internal/notify: TestSendFallsBackOnRecipientNotFound, TestDedupFamilyWindow, TestRateLimit, TestUnknownRecipientSendsNothing, TestObsoleteAndBlockedSuppressed, TestRetryAfterHonoured (fake clock), TestSurvivesRestart, TestTemplatesGolden, TestNoEmailInLogsOrFindings.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given channels [a, b] where a returns ErrRecipientNotFound, the dispatcher calls a once and b once and the row ends state sent with last_outcome fallback then sent: `go test ./internal/notify -run TestSendFallsBackOnRecipientNotFound`
- [ ] Given Send(connect_link, U, pending:P) at t0, Send(park_pending, U, pending:P) at t0+5m and Send(connect_link, U, pending:P) at t0+11m, exactly 2 deliveries happen and the middle call returns outcome deduped: `go test ./internal/notify -run TestDedupFamilyWindow`
- [ ] Given 11 Sends with distinct refs for one user_key within 5 minutes, 10 are delivered and the 11th returns rate_limited: `go test ./internal/notify -run TestRateLimit`
- [ ] Given a queued row and a new Service opened on the same cpstate DB after the first is stopped, the message is delivered exactly once; if the resolver reports the ref completed, it is marked obsolete and nothing is sent: `go test ./internal/notify -run TestSurvivesRestart`
- [ ] Given a canary email and an auth failure on every channel, the notify_channel_down Finding, the outbox row and captured logs contain neither the email nor the error text: `go test ./internal/notify -run TestNoEmailInLogsOrFindings`
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/notify/...` passes

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-NTFY-01`](user-notify.md#110--w-p4-ntfy-01) Add UserNotifier capability, typed delivery errors and user-notifier binding; [`W-P4-NTFY-07`](user-notify.md#710--w-p4-ntfy-07) Add verified user contacts table keyed by user_key; [`W-P1-SSO-01`](console-sso-rbac.md#18--w-p1-sso-01) Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations; [`W-P1-BLOCK-03`](user-block-list.md#310--w-p1-block-03) Add the CP block-list store, admin API and policy merge

### 5/10 · W-P4-NTFY-05

**Send connect-link notifications from JIT pending creation**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#219](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/219)

Hook the connect_link kind into the create branch of W-P3-JIT-01's create-or-reuse path in internal/oauthbroker, so a user hit by a missing grant gets a DM or email with the portal link. The message is built only from the stored pending row and registry data, never from text the agent or worker supplied (carry-forward from p3-jit). Enqueue is one INSERT after the pending commits and never fails or delays the response to the worker. The portal landing page shows whether the user was notified.

**Requirements**

- Send(connect_link) runs only when W-P3-JIT-01 inserts a new pending row, never on reuse, already_granted or the ON CONFLICT re-select, and only when notifications.enabled and notifications.kinds.connect_link are true.
- Params come only from the pending_authorizations row: user_key, agent_id (rendered with the W-P2-AREG registry display name), provider (rendered with its configured display name), scopes, request method, request host and expires_at. request_path, mcp_tool arguments, reason, message and any worker- or agent-supplied text are never used. Ref is pending:<pending_id>.
- The link is consent.publicURL + /portal/connect/<pending_id> (the W-P3-PORT-03 landing page) and never carries status_token. The landing page's owner check stays the access control.
- An enqueue error never changes the pending response status or body; it is logged without user data and counted as outcome enqueue_failed.
- A pending RefResolver is registered with notify: a pending is actionable while status is pending and expires_at is in the future.
- The PORT-03 landing page and its API show the latest outbox outcome for ref pending:<id> (sent, pending, failed or not sent) and the channel type (slack or email, not the instance name), visible only to the pending's owner; others get the existing 404. Rendering uses textContent only.
- Exactly one message per pending: a cpstate migration on pending_authorizations (W-P3-BRKR-02) adds notified_at, notify_kind and notify_status, and the producer sends only after `GrantStore.MarkNotified(ctx, id)` wins `UPDATE ... SET notified_at=? WHERE id=? AND notified_at IS NULL` (rows affected == 1). The kind comes from a `KindSelector(row) Kind` seam that defaults to connect_link; W-P4-PARK-02 installs the park selector instead of adding a second send path, so connect_link and park_pending never both go out for one pending.

**Implementation plan**

1. Edit internal/oauthbroker (the W-P3-JIT-01 handler): add an optional Notifier seam (interface with Send) and call it in the create branch after commit.
2. Add the pending RefResolver in internal/oauthbroker over the W-P3-BRKR-02 pending store and register it with notify.Service during CP wiring in internal/controlplane.
3. Edit internal/portal (W-P3-PORT-03 landing handler and template): read the latest outbox row by ref through a small notify.StatusReader interface and render the status.
4. Tests: internal/oauthbroker TestJITPendingNotifiesOnce, TestJITNotifyDisabled, TestJITNotifyUsesPendingColumnsOnly, TestJITNotifyFailureDoesNotFailPending; internal/portal TestPendingNotificationStatus.
5. Add the notified_at, notify_kind and notify_status migration, GrantStore.MarkNotified (CAS) and the KindSelector seam in internal/oauthbroker; record notify_status from the Send outcome. Test TestJITNotifyCASOnce: 20 racing creates and reuses for one pending produce one outbox row.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given kinds.connect_link true and a JIT miss that creates a pending, exactly one connect_link Send occurs with ref pending:<id>; a second miss that reuses the pending adds no outbox row: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestJITPendingNotifiesOnce`
- [ ] Given the notifications block absent or kinds.connect_link false, creating a pending writes no outbox row: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestJITNotifyDisabled`
- [ ] Given a worker request with path "/x?<a href=evil>" and reason scope_insufficient, the rendered text and HTML contain neither "/x" nor "evil", and the action URL equals publicURL/portal/connect/<id> with no query: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestJITNotifyUsesPendingColumnsOnly`
- [ ] Given a Notifier whose Send returns an error, the pending endpoint still returns 201 with the same body: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestJITNotifyFailureDoesNotFailPending`
- [ ] Given one sent and one dead notification for two pendings, each landing page shows sent and failed respectively, and another user's session gets 404: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPendingNotificationStatus`

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-NTFY-08`](user-notify.md#810--w-p4-ntfy-08) Add CP-local notifications config block and CP wiring; [`W-P3-JIT-01`](jit-authorization.md#17--w-p3-jit-01) Add CP endpoint to create or reuse pending authorizations; [`W-P3-PORT-03`](consent-portal.md#37--w-p3-port-03) Add the pending landing page and connect, continue and decline actions; [`W-P2-AREG-01`](agent-registry.md#17--w-p2-areg-01) Add internal/agentreg store, schema and validation

### 6/10 · W-P4-NTFY-06

**Add console notification settings, preview, test-send and delivery counters**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#220](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/220)

Add an admin-only console page to read and write the notifications block, preview each kind with fixture data, and send a test message to the signed-in admin. Show per-channel delivery counters next to the existing integration instance status so retries, fallbacks and dedup are visible. Template editing and per-user preferences are out of scope here. The ticket is CP-only.

**Requirements**

- GET and PUT /dashboard/api/notifications (admin role in the W-P1-SSO-05 route table, audited by W-P1-AAUD-02) read and write enabled, channels, kinds, dedupWindow, perUserLimit, maxAttemptAge and retention. A new Server.WriteNotifications mirrors WriteIntegrations: it changes only this block, re-runs structural validation and SupportsUserNotify (400 notification_channel_invalid naming the channel), and hot-swaps the Service config.

3. internal/controlplane authz table: add the new routes as admin with Audited true.
4. internal/dashboard/dashboard_integrations.go: extend IntegrationInstanceStatus with capabilities and counters from a notify.Stats interface; update the integrations tab UI.

### 7/10 · W-P4-NTFY-07

**Add verified user contacts table keyed by user_key**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#309](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/309)

No earlier ticket stores a durable, verified email per user: idp_links exists only when IdP linking is on, portal sessions expire, and a user hit by a JIT miss may never have signed in to the portal. Add a cpstate user_contacts table keyed by secrets.UserKey(iss, sub), written only from verified identities, so notify can find a recipient. Writes are behind the notifications enabled flag and never fail a login or a pending.

**Requirements**

- cpstate migration `contacts/0001`: user_contacts(user_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, iss, sub, email, email_verified INTEGER, source TEXT CHECK in (portal, console, jit), updated_at). user_key is computed only with secrets.UserKey (W-P3-CSIG-06).
- New package internal/contacts with Store.Upsert(ctx, Entry), Get(ctx, userKey) (Entry, bool, error) and Delete(ctx, userKey), and a Directory interface for internal/notify.
- Email is lowercased and stored only when email_verified is true; an unverified identity never overwrites a stored verified email.
- Upserts come from the portal callback (W-P3-CSIG-02), the console OIDC callback (W-P1-SSO-03) and W-P3-JIT-01 pending creation, which uses the email and email_verified claims of the CP-re-verified Warden token (W-P2-TOKX-02). Failures are logged without the email and never fail the caller.
- The offboarding contain step (W-P3-OFFB-01) calls Delete for the user. Rows are written only when notifications.enabled is true.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/contacts/store.go: migration registered for cpstate.Open, Store and Directory.
2. Edit internal/portal (W-P3-CSIG-02 callback) and the console OIDC callback (W-P1-SSO-03) to call an optional ContactRecorder seam after admission.
3. Edit internal/oauthbroker (W-P3-JIT-01 handler) to call the same seam with the verified token claims.
4. Edit the Offboarder (W-P3-OFFB-01) to call Delete in the contain step through an optional seam.
5. Tests: internal/contacts TestUpsertVerifiedOnly, TestUnverifiedKeepsVerified, TestDelete; internal/portal TestCallbackRecordsContact; internal/oauthbroker TestJITRecordsContact.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given an upsert with email_verified false for a new user, no email is stored; given a later unverified upsert for a user with a verified email, the verified email is kept: `go test ./internal/contacts -run 'TestUpsertVerifiedOnly|TestUnverifiedKeepsVerified'`
- [ ] Given a portal login for alice with a verified email and notifications enabled, user_contacts has one row with user_key = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) and source portal: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestCallbackRecordsContact`
- [ ] Given a JIT pending created for a token with a verified email, a jit row exists; with notifications disabled no row is written: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestJITRecordsContact`
- [ ] Given a contact store that returns an error, login and pending creation still succeed and logs contain no email: `go test ./internal/contacts/... ./internal/portal/... -run ContactFailure`

### 8/10 · W-P4-NTFY-08

**Add CP-local notifications config block and CP wiring**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#310](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/310)

Add the default-off `notifications:` block next to `integrations:` and wire notify.Service, the dispatcher and the contacts recorder into the CP when it is enabled. Capability checks run at CP wiring through SupportsUserNotify because internal/config does not import internal/integration. The block is CP-local (json:"-") and every existing writer keeps it byte-identical. With the block absent nothing new starts.

**Requirements**

- config.Policy gains Notifications (json:"-") parsed from a raw struct with KnownFields: enabled (false), channels (max 4, unique, each present in integrations), kinds (bool per kind, each default false even with enabled true; a producer whose kind is false writes no outbox row), dedupWindow (10m), perUserLimit {count 10, window 5m}, maxAttemptAge (15m), retention (720h).
- WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteIntegrations, WriteDetection and the llm-providers writer keep the notifications node byte-identical, and it never appears on policyWire or SettingsWire.
- When enabled, the CP requires --state-dir and consent.publicURL (W-P3-JIT-01), and every channel's type must pass integration.SupportsUserNotify; otherwise startup fails naming the field or channel.
- internal/controlplane builds notify.Service with ChannelSource over alertpipeline.Pipeline.CurrentManager(), the contacts Directory, a BlockStore Suppressor, and publicURL; starts the dispatcher; registers the contacts recorder seams; and adds outbox pruning to the CP retention ticker.
- With the block absent or enabled false, no notify migration effect, goroutine or contact write exists, and /policy bytes are unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/config/notifications.go: Notifications type, raw struct, defaults and validateNotifications; hook into the existing load path next to parseIntegrations.
2. Edit internal/config wire builders and the controlplane writers to preserve the block; add tests next to the existing round-trip tests.
3. Edit internal/controlplane/controlplane.go New: build and start notify.Service and the dispatcher, register seams, stop them on shutdown.
4. Tests: internal/config TestNotificationsConfig, TestNotificationsNotOnWire; internal/controlplane TestWritersPreserveNotificationsBlock, TestNotificationsChannelCapability, TestNotifyDisabledByDefault.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given channels naming an instance absent from integrations, config load fails naming it: `go test ./internal/config -run TestNotificationsConfig`
- [ ] Given notifications and slack/email instances with ${ENV} secrets, the marshalled policyWire and SettingsWire contain no notifications key, botToken or password: `go test ./internal/config -run TestNotificationsNotOnWire`
- [ ] Given channels listing a webhook instance, CP startup fails with an error naming that instance: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestNotificationsChannelCapability`
- [ ] Given the block absent, no notify.Service is built, /policy bytes match the pre-change golden, and WriteIntegrations round-trips the file byte-identically: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestNotifyDisabledByDefault|TestWritersPreserveNotificationsBlock'`
- [ ] Given `notifications: {enabled: true, channels: [slack]}` with no kinds, every kind parses as false and no producer writes an outbox row: `go test ./internal/config -run TestNotificationsKindsDefaultFalse`.

### 9/10 · W-P4-NTFY-09

**Add per-user channel order preference in the portal**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#311](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/311)

Let a signed-in portal user choose whether Slack or email is tried first for their messages. The user can only reorder channel types the operator configured, never add a channel or turn off delivery. This was split out of the original console ticket because it is a separate portal surface with its own session and CSRF handling.

**Requirements**

- cpstate migration `notify/0002`: notify_prefs(user_key PRIMARY KEY, order_json, updated_at).
- GET and PUT /portal/api/notifications/preference behind the portal session middleware with CSRF (W-P3-CSIG-04), scoped to the session's user_key. The body is an ordered list of channel types (slack, email); unknown values or duplicates return 400.
- The dispatcher reorders the configured channels by the user's preference, keeping only configured channels; with no preference the configured order is used.
- The portal page (W-P3-PORT-01) shows the control only when notifications are enabled and more than one channel type is configured.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/notify: add the notify/0002 migration and a PrefStore; apply the order in the dispatcher's channel walk.
2. internal/portal: add the two handlers and the page control.
3. Tests: internal/notify TestPreferenceReordersChain, TestPreferenceCannotAddChannel; internal/portal TestPreferenceRequiresCSRF, TestPreferenceScopedToUser.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given channels [slack, email] and a preference [email, slack], the dispatcher calls email first for that user only: `go test ./internal/notify -run TestPreferenceReordersChain`
- [ ] Given a PUT with ["webhook"], the API returns 400 and nothing is stored: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPreferenceCannotAddChannel`
- [ ] Given a PUT without a CSRF token, the API returns 403: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPreferenceRequiresCSRF`

### 10/10 · W-P4-NTFY-10

**Add end-to-end test for connect-link notifications with fallback**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#312](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/312)

Prove the feature's done_when with an in-process CP, a fake Slack API and a fake SMTP server. The test covers DM delivery with a working portal link, email fallback, dedup, survival across a CP restart, suppression for blocked users, and the counters in the integrations status. It changes no production code.

**Requirements**

- Test under the integration build tag in internal/controlplane/notify_e2e_test.go with consent, JIT, notifications enabled (channels [slack, email], kinds.connect_link true), slack pointed at an httptest fake and email at the fake TLS SMTP server from W-P4-NTFY-03.
- Covers: one DM with button URL publicURL/portal/connect/<id>; email fallback when the fake Slack returns users_not_found; no second message within 10 minutes; delivery after a CP restart while both channels failed; obsolete when the pending completed; nothing for a blocked user.
- Asserts that no captured payload, log line or Finding contains the subject token, status_token, the request path or query, or another user's email.
- Asserts GET /dashboard/api/integrations shows sent, fallback, retried, dead and deduped counts.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/controlplane/notify_e2e_test.go: start the CP with the fakes and a seeded contact, then create pendings through POST /control/connect/pending.
2. Drive each scenario in sub-tests and restart the CP on the same --state-dir for the restart case.
3. Scan captured fake payloads, slog output and published Findings for the canary values.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags integration ./internal/controlplane -run TestNotifyE2E` passes.
- [ ] The restart sub-test delivers exactly one message after restart and the obsolete sub-test delivers none.
- [ ] The canary scan sub-test finds no token, status_token, path, query or foreign email in any captured output.
